lessons.title: Bonding, formulae and balanced reactions
objectives: Explain ionic and covalent models.
Derive simple neutral formulae and empirical ratios.
Balance equations without changing substances.
paragraphs: Chemical bonds hold particles together. In ionic, or electrovalent, bonding, electron transfer produces oppositely charged ions whose electrostatic attraction holds a structure together. A sodium atom can lose one electron to become Na⁺, while chlorine gains one to become Cl⁻. Sodium chloride is an extended ionic structure, not a collection of separate NaCl molecules. Its formula describes a 1:1 ratio of ions.

In a covalent bond, atoms share one or more pairs of electrons. H₂ has a shared pair between hydrogen atoms, O₂ is represented with a double bond and N₂ with a triple bond in introductory models. Many simple covalent substances consist of molecules; network structures such as diamond are exceptions. Ionic substances often conduct when molten or dissolved because ions can move, but do not normally conduct as solids. These patterns depend on structure rather than a label alone.

A compound formula must balance charges when it represents an electrically neutral ionic substance. Calcium is Ca²⁺ and chloride is Cl⁻, so the ratio is one calcium to two chloride ions: CaCl₂. For aluminium oxide, Al³⁺ and O²⁻ require two aluminium ions and three oxide ions, giving Al₂O₃. An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms; a molecular formula gives actual atom numbers in a molecule. Glucose has molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆ and empirical formula CH₂O.

A chemical equation represents a reaction while conserving atoms. Change coefficients before formulae to balance it; changing a subscript changes the substance. For hydrogen burning, 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms on each side. Combination reactions join reactants into a product; decomposition breaks a reactant into products; displacement replaces one element in a compound. A reaction can fit more than one useful description, so define the classification being used.
examples: Balance Mg + O₂ → MgO: put 2 before MgO to obtain two oxygen atoms on the right, then 2 before Mg. Result: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
Derive magnesium chloride: Mg²⁺ needs two Cl⁻ ions to make zero net charge. Write MgCl₂, not Mg₂Cl. The ratio follows the charges.
C₂H₆ has ratio C:H of 2:6. Divide by 2 to obtain empirical formula CH₃. The molecular formula still contains two carbon and six hydrogen atoms.

lessons.title: Current, voltage and resistance
objectives: Use current, voltage and resistance relations.
Compare series and parallel circuits.
Calculate electrical energy and apply safe boundaries.
paragraphs: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge: I = Q/t, measured in amperes (A). Conventional current is described in the direction positive charge would move. In a metal, electrons drift in the opposite direction. A simple circuit needs a complete conducting path and an energy source. Current is not used up by a lamp; energy is transferred in the lamp while charge continues around the circuit.

Potential difference, or voltage, is energy transferred per unit charge: V = E/Q. A voltmeter is connected across a component in parallel. An ammeter measures current and is connected in series. Resistance describes opposition to current, R = V/I, measured in ohms (Ω). For an ohmic conductor at constant temperature, V is proportional to I. A lamp filament can heat up and change resistance, so not every component gives a straight-line V–I graph.

In a series path, the same current passes through each component and potential differences add across the supply. For resistors, total series resistance is R₁ + R₂ + …. In parallel branches, the voltage is the same across each branch and branch currents add to the supply current. These statements require a correctly identified circuit; drawing components near each other does not prove they are in series or parallel.

Electrical power can be calculated as P = VI. Energy transferred at constant power is E = Pt. Use seconds for joules, or use kilowatts and hours for kilowatt-hours. Household mains electricity is dangerous. Independent school-level experiments should use only teacher-approved low-voltage supplies; never experiment on wall sockets, household wiring or damaged appliances. Fuses and circuit breakers can interrupt excessive current, but are not permission to handle live equipment.
examples: A charge of 120 C passes in 30 s. Current I=120/30=4 A.
A resistor has 6 V across it and 0.5 A through it. R=6/0.5=12 Ω. Power P=6×0.5=3 W.
A 60 W lamp operates for 2 h. Energy = 0.060 kW × 2 h = 0.12 kWh. In joules, 60 × 7200 = 432,000 J.
lessons.summary: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge: I = Q/t, measured in amperes (A).

lessons.title: Transport in flowering plants and humans
objectives: Explain transport tissues and transpiration.
Trace double circulation and blood components.
Interpret controlled transport and pulse observations.
paragraphs: Flowering plants use xylem to transport water and dissolved mineral ions mainly from roots towards leaves. Root hairs increase contact area with soil water. Osmosis is net water movement through a partially permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to lower water potential. Mineral-ion uptake and water uptake should not be treated as exactly the same process; active transport can contribute to ion uptake.

Transpiration is water-vapour loss from aerial plant parts, especially leaves. Evaporation from leaf surfaces and diffusion out through stomata contribute to the process. A transpiration pull helps move a continuous water column through xylem. Warmer, drier or windier conditions often increase water loss, while stomatal closure can limit it. Phloem transports sugars and other organic substances between sources and sinks, not simply water upwards.

In humans, the heart pumps blood through a double circulation: blood passes through the lungs and through the rest of the body in separate circuits. The right side receives blood returning from the body and pumps it to the lungs; the left side receives blood from the lungs and pumps it to the body. The left ventricle has a thicker muscular wall because the systemic circuit requires higher pressure. Valves help prevent backward flow.

Arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry it towards the heart; these definitions concern direction, not oxygen content. The pulmonary artery carries blood low in oxygen to the lungs, while pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood. Capillaries have thin walls for exchange with tissues. Red blood cells carry oxygen with haemoglobin, white blood cells support defence, platelets support clotting and plasma transports dissolved substances.

A pulse is the pressure wave felt in an artery when the heart beats. To compare pulse rate before and after ordinary activity, use the same measurement duration and conditions, count carefully and allow recovery. Avoid strenuous exercise tests for anyone with health concerns; use supplied data instead. A short classroom observation is not a medical diagnosis, and unexpected symptoms should be addressed by a responsible adult and a qualified health professional.
examples: A pulse count of 18 beats in 15 s corresponds to 18×4=72 beats/min. Multiplying is appropriate only if that short interval represents the rate being estimated.

A leafy shoot loses water faster in moving dry air than in still humid air under otherwise similar conditions. This supports a role for diffusion conditions, but does not isolate wind if humidity also changed.
Trace circulation: body → right heart → lungs → left heart → body. Place oxygen uptake at the lungs and delivery to tissues in the systemic circulation.
lessons.summary: Flowering plants use xylem to transport water and dissolved mineral ions mainly from roots towards leaves.

lessons.title: Sets and right-triangle trigonometry
objectives: Perform and explain two-set operations.
Count overlapping set memberships.
Use right-triangle ratios and elevation/depression diagrams.
paragraphs: A set is a well-defined collection of distinct elements. Write A={1,2,3}; repeating an element does not increase the set size. The empty set has no elements, and a universal set U gives the context in which complements are taken. Equal sets have exactly the same elements; equivalent finite sets have the same number of elements but need not contain the same things. A subset contains only elements of another set.

The union A∪B includes elements in either set or both. The intersection A∩B includes elements common to both. The complement A′ includes elements of U that are not in A, so its meaning depends on the chosen universal set. For two finite sets, n(A∪B)=n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B). Subtract the intersection because it was counted twice. A Venn diagram should show overlapping regions and the relevant universe clearly.

In a right-angled triangle, choose an acute angle θ. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle and is the longest side; the opposite and adjacent sides are named relative to θ. Define sin θ=opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ=adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ=opposite/adjacent. Changing the chosen acute angle changes which shorter side is opposite and which is adjacent.

An angle of elevation is measured upwards from the horizontal line of sight; an angle of depression is measured downwards from a horizontal line. Draw the horizontal explicitly rather than measuring from a vertical wall. Choose a ratio that uses the known and required sides. These ratios apply directly to right triangles; do not apply them blindly to a triangle with no right angle. If a calculator is used for ordinary angle problems, ensure its angle mode matches degrees.
examples: If A={1,2,3} and B={3,4}, then A∪B={1,2,3,4} and A∩B={3}. Their sizes are 4 and 1, and 3+2−1=4.
In a 3–4–5 right triangle, choose θ opposite the side of length 3. Then sin θ=3/5, cos θ=4/5 and tan θ=3/4.

A vertical pole is observed from 10 m away at 45° elevation on level ground. tan45°=height/10=1, so the height above the observation level is 10 m. Add observer eye height only if the question requires height above ground.
lessons.summary: A set is a well-defined collection of distinct elements.

lessons.title: Photograph interpretation and geographical evidence
objectives: Distinguish photographic views and image regions.
Separate observation from interpretation.
Explain scale, timing and comparison limitations.
paragraphs: A geographical photograph records a selected view at a particular time and location. Ground photographs are taken near ground level; aerial photographs are taken from above and can be vertical or oblique. A photograph is not a map with a single uniform scale. Perspective, camera angle and distance can make apparent sizes misleading, especially in oblique views.

In a ground or oblique view, the foreground is nearest the camera, the middle ground lies farther away and the background is most distant. Describe location using these regions and relative positions before interpreting features. A river, terrace, road or settlement may be recognised through shape, pattern and associations, but a single image may not reveal names, exact dimensions or the date of an activity.

Observation states what is visible; interpretation proposes its geographical meaning. Parallel lines of plants may suggest cultivated land, but the crop species should not be named without sufficient evidence. Roof clusters connected by paths may suggest a settlement; their existence alone does not prove income level or population size. Use cautious claims and compare with maps, field information or other images when possible.

Photographs can support studies of land use, erosion, transport, vegetation and change. A before-and-after comparison needs comparable viewpoints, dates and seasonal conditions. A dry-season image and a wet-season image might show vegetation differences without proving permanent deforestation. Cropping can hide important context, so record the source, date if known and limitations instead of treating a photograph as a complete account.
examples: Visible parallel rows and cleared soil support an interpretation of cultivation. Without closer evidence, identifying the field as maize rather than another crop is an unsupported extra claim.
A road appears wider in the foreground than in the background. Perspective can explain the difference; it does not necessarily mean the real road narrows by the same proportion.
Two images of a river taken at different seasons show different water levels. Check dates and rainfall before concluding that the change was caused by a dam.
lessons.summary: A geographical photograph records a selected view at a particular time and location.

lessons.title: Business records, budgets and local opportunities
objectives: Keep basic cash and credit records.
Compare budgets and actual outcomes.
Evaluate local opportunities using evidence and responsibilities.
paragraphs: Management coordinates people, money, materials and activities to reach a business objective. Planning decides what should be done, organising arranges resources, directing supports implementation and controlling compares actual results with the plan. These functions overlap in a small enterprise, where the owner may perform several roles. A written plan is useful only if it is checked against real results.

Records should distinguish cash received, cash paid, credit transactions, goods held and debts. A simple receipt record does not reveal every cost or obligation. For a credit customer, write the date, amount owed, agreed payment date and later payments so the balance can be checked. Keep evidence securely and respect customer privacy. Never invent receipts or erase differences to make a record appear correct.

A budget estimates income and spending for a stated period. A cash-flow plan pays attention to when money is received and paid, not just total profit. A business may expect profitable sales but run short of cash if suppliers must be paid before customers pay. Compare actual figures with budgeted figures and investigate significant differences. Use the comparison to improve estimates rather than treat a budget as a guaranteed prediction.

Local opportunities can arise from unmet needs, changes in transport, seasonal demand, repair needs or improved ways of doing existing work. Assess demand, resources, competitors, likely costs and relevant requirements. Social and environmental effects also matter: a low-cost business that creates unsafe waste or exploits customers is not automatically a sound opportunity. An evidence-based small test can reveal whether the opportunity is practical before committing all available resources.
examples: A shop starts with TSh 25,000, receives 18,000 cash and pays 31,000. Closing cash=25,000+18,000−31,000=12,000. Credit sales unpaid at this date are not added as cash receipts.
A customer owes TSh 15,000 and pays 6000. Outstanding debt=9000. Recording the payment twice would falsely reduce the balance.
Budgeted transport was TSh 8000 and actual cost 9500. Actual spending exceeded budget by TSh 1500. Investigate price, distance and trip count before assigning a cause.
lessons.summary: Management coordinates people, money, materials and activities to reach a business objective.

lessons.title: Uhuru, Mapinduzi na ujenzi wa Taifa
objectives: Panga matukio ya uhuru, jamhuri, Mapinduzi na Muungano.
Chunguza changamoto na mikakati ya 1961–1966.
Tofautisha malengo, ushahidi na matokeo.
paragraphs: Uhuru hubadili mamlaka ya kisiasa lakini hauondoi mara moja matatizo yote ya uchumi na jamii. Tanganyika ilipopata uhuru mwaka 1961, serikali na wananchi walikabiliwa na mahitaji ya elimu, afya, miundombinu, watumishi wenye ujuzi na kupunguza tofauti zilizorithiwa. Kuchunguza kipindi cha 1961–1966 kunahitaji kutofautisha malengo, hatua zilizochukuliwa na matokeo yake badala ya kudhani kila lengo lilitimia mara moja.

Maendeleo ya utaifa yalihusisha kuimarisha ushirikiano wa watu wa maeneo, lugha na dini tofauti. Kiswahili kilichangia mawasiliano ya kitaifa, huku taasisi na shughuli za pamoja zikitoa nafasi za kujenga mshikamano. Utaifa unaoheshimu watu hauhitaji kudharau tofauti zao. Maadili kama uadilifu, uwajibikaji na usawa ni muhimu wakati wa kutumia rasilimali na kujenga huduma kwa wote.

Tanganyika ilikuwa jamhuri kuanzia tarehe 9 Desemba 1962, mwaka mmoja baada ya uhuru. Zanzibar ilipata uhuru tarehe 10 Desemba 1963 na Mapinduzi yakatokea tarehe 12 Januari 1964. Chimbuko la Mapinduzi linahitaji kuchunguzwa katika muktadha wa tofauti za kijamii na kiuchumi, mashindano ya kisiasa na malalamiko kuhusu utawala na uwakilishi. Eleza madai kwa ushahidi na epuka kuwahusisha watu wote wa kundi fulani na msimamo mmoja.

Muungano wa Tanganyika na Zanzibar ulifanyika tarehe 26 Aprili 1964. Kuunganisha maeneo hayo kulifungua hatua mpya katika ujenzi wa Taifa, lakini si kila suala la maisha na utawala lilikuwa sawa pande zote. Tathmini mchango wa umoja na changamoto zake kwa vyanzo vinavyotaja wakati na eneo. Usihamishe sera za baadaye na kuzitaja kana kwamba zilitangazwa kabla ya 1966: kwa mfano Azimio la Arusha lilitangazwa mwaka 1967, nje ya kipindi hicho cha awali.
examples: Mpangilio: uhuru wa Tanganyika 1961 → jamhuri 1962 → uhuru wa Zanzibar 1963 → Mapinduzi na Muungano 1964. Mfuatano unaonyesha tofauti za matukio yanayokaribiana.
Tathmini ya huduma za elimu inaanza kwa kutaja hitaji, hatua na ushahidi wa matokeo. Kutangaza lengo la kujenga shule si sawa na kuthibitisha kwamba kila mtoto alipata nafasi mara moja.
Kauli Azimio la Arusha lilikuwa sehemu ya hatua za 1961–1966 ina kosa la kipindi. Azimio lilitangazwa 1967; linaweza kutajwa kama tukio linalofuata, si la ndani ya kipindi hicho.
lessons.summary: Uhuru hubadili mamlaka ya kisiasa lakini hauondoi mara moja matatizo yote ya uchumi na jamii.

lessons.title: Insha za hoja, wasifu na muhtasari
objectives: Jenga insha zenye hoja na mpangilio.
Andika wasifu unaoheshimu ukweli na faragha.
Fupisha matini na rekodi maamuzi bila kubuni.
paragraphs: Insha ya hoja huwasilisha msimamo kuhusu suala na kuujenga kwa sababu, mifano na ushahidi. Utangulizi hutambulisha suala; kiini huendeleza hoja katika aya; hitimisho huunganisha msimamo na hoja bila kuleta mada mpya isiyojadiliwa. Mwandishi anaweza kutaja hoja pinzani kwa haki, kisha kueleza kwa nini ushahidi wake unaunga mkono msimamo aliouchagua.

Insha ya wasifu humweleza mtu, mahali, kitu au hali kwa vipengele vinavyojenga picha yenye mpangilio. Maelezo yawe na kusudi badala ya kuwa orodha ya vivumishi. Kwa mtu, chagua taarifa zinazofaa na zinazoheshimu faragha; usibuni sifa au matendo na kuyawasilisha kama ukweli. Kwa mahali, unaweza kufuata mpangilio kutoka eneo pana kwenda sehemu maalumu au kutoka nje kwenda ndani.

Soma matini hii asilia: Shule yetu ilianzisha kikundi cha kusoma wakati wa mapumziko. Mwanzoni wanafunzi wachache walihudhuria kwa sababu wengi hawakujua mpango huo. Wanakikundi waliweka ratiba ubaoni na kuomba ruhusa ya kutumia kivuli karibu na maktaba. Baada ya wiki mbili, walipata washiriki zaidi. Hata hivyo, baadhi walilalamika kwamba muda ulikuwa mfupi. Kikundi kikapendekeza vipindi viwili kwa wiki badala ya kipindi kimoja. Mabadiliko hayo yalihitaji makubaliano ili yasiingiliane na shughuli nyingine za shule.

Muhtasari huchagua mawazo makuu na kuyaeleza kwa ufupi bila kubadili maana. Katika matini ya kikundi, hoja kuu ni kuanzishwa kwa kikundi, hatua za kufahamisha wengine, ongezeko la washiriki na pendekezo la kuboresha muda. Kutaja kwamba kikundi kilikuwa na washiriki mia moja kungebuni taarifa ambayo haikutolewa. Kumbukumbu za mjadala zinaweza kuonyesha suala, hoja kuu, uamuzi na kazi iliyokabidhiwa; zitofautishe pendekezo ambalo bado halijakubaliwa na uamuzi wa mwisho.
examples: Hoja: Ratiba iliyo wazi husaidia ushiriki. Sababu: wanafunzi wanajua muda na mahali. Ushahidi wa matini: washiriki waliongezeka baada ya ratiba kuwekwa na taarifa kutolewa.
Muhtasari: Kikundi cha kusoma kiliongeza ushiriki kwa kutoa taarifa na ratiba, kisha kikapendekeza vipindi zaidi ili kukabiliana na muda mfupi. Hatujatoa idadi ya washiriki ambayo haikutajwa.
Kumbukumbu sahihi: Pendekezo la vipindi viwili litatathminiwa. Kumbukumbu isiyo sahihi: Vipindi viwili vimeidhinishwa. Matini imetaja pendekezo linalohitaji makubaliano, si kibali cha mwisho.
lessons.summary: Insha ya hoja huwasilisha msimamo kuhusu suala na kuujenga kwa sababu, mifano na ushahidi.

lessons.title: Requests, claims and email messages
objectives: Write clear requests, claims and email subjects.
Distinguish proposals from agreements.
Use respectful language and protect private information.
paragraphs: A formal request states who is writing, what is needed and why the request is reasonable. Use a suitable greeting, an organised message and a respectful closing. Being formal does not require long or difficult words. A school request for equipment should identify the items, their purpose and any relevant timing; it should not imply approval has already been given.

A claim letter raises an issue and asks for a remedy based on evidence. Explain the transaction or event, describe the problem accurately, include relevant details such as a date or receipt reference and state the action requested. Avoid threats or unsupported accusations. Keep personal details to what is necessary. A copy of a receipt can support a claim, but the original should normally be retained safely.

An email needs a clear subject line as well as its body. Check the recipient, spelling, attachments and whether private information should be sent. A subject such as Request for footballs for the school team is more useful than Hello. Do not write Attached is the list if no list is actually attached. Messages in group contexts also need turn-taking: acknowledge the previous point before changing topics or disagreeing.

Read this original model: Dear Head Teacher, Our science club requests permission to use the classroom on Friday from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m. We plan to revise measurement questions in small groups. A club leader will record attendance and ensure the room is left tidy. Please let us know whether the room is available. Yours faithfully, The Science Club. The message gives a purpose, time, responsibility and a clear request; it does not assume permission.

Polite negotiation uses clear proposals and reasons: Could you offer a lower price if we buy several items? A seller may accept, refuse or propose another amount. Agreement requires both sides to understand the item, quantity, price and terms. Politeness supports communication but does not oblige another person to accept an offer. Keep a request distinct from a demand and a proposal distinct from a confirmed agreement.
examples: Unclear subject: Request. Improved subject: Request to use classroom on Friday, 3–4 p.m. The improved version lets the recipient identify the action quickly.

Accusatory claim: You cheated me. Evidence-based claim: The notebook has several missing pages. I bought it yesterday and would like a replacement; the receipt number is 18. The second states the problem and requested remedy.

Negotiation: Could you sell three notebooks for TSh 4200? Seller: I can offer three for TSh 4500. Buyer: Thank you; I accept that price. The final acceptance, not the first proposal, establishes agreement here.
lessons.summary: A formal request states who is writing, what is needed and why the request is reasonable.

questions.content: What is shared in a covalent bond?
questions.answerKey: A pair of electrons.
questions.markingGuide: A single covalent bond involves one shared pair. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What holds oppositely charged ions together?
questions.answerKey: Electrostatic attraction.
questions.markingGuide: This is the basis of ionic bonding. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Write the formula from Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻.
questions.answerKey: MgCl₂
questions.markingGuide: Two chloride ions balance one magnesium ion. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Write the formula from Al³⁺ and O²⁻.
questions.answerKey: Al₂O₃
questions.markingGuide: Total positive and negative charges are both six in magnitude. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find the empirical formula of C₄H₈.
questions.answerKey: CH₂
questions.markingGuide: Divide both subscripts by four. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find the empirical formula of C₆H₁₂O₆.
questions.answerKey: CH₂O
questions.markingGuide: Divide every subscript by six. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Balance H₂ + Cl₂ → HCl.
questions.answerKey: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl
questions.markingGuide: Both sides then have two H and two Cl atoms. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Balance N₂ + H₂ → NH₃.
questions.answerKey: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃
questions.markingGuide: Both sides have two N and six H atoms. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why must subscripts not be changed to balance an equation?
questions.answerKey: They define the substances; changing them changes chemical identity.
questions.markingGuide: Balance by changing coefficients instead. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Classify 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO as combination or decomposition.
questions.answerKey: Combination.
questions.markingGuide: Two reactants form one product substance. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Classify CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.
questions.answerKey: Decomposition.
questions.markingGuide: One reactant breaks into more than one product substance. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why can molten sodium chloride conduct electricity?
questions.answerKey: Its ions are mobile and can carry charge.
questions.markingGuide: Solid-state ions are not free to move throughout the structure. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Does NaCl describe a separate molecule in the ordinary solid?
questions.answerKey: No; it gives the ratio in an extended ionic structure.
questions.markingGuide: Do not confuse formula unit with molecule. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Distinguish empirical and molecular formula.
questions.answerKey: Empirical is the simplest atom ratio; molecular gives actual atom counts per molecule.
questions.markingGuide: Give a linked example such as CH₂O and C₆H₁₂O₆. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Count oxygen atoms on each side of 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
questions.answerKey: Two on each side.
questions.markingGuide: The coefficient multiplies the complete formula. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find current if 90 C passes in 15 s.
questions.answerKey: 6 A
questions.markingGuide: I=Q/t. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: State the unit of potential difference.
questions.answerKey: Volt (V).
questions.markingGuide: A volt equals a joule per coulomb. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: How is an ammeter connected?
questions.answerKey: In series with the component/path.
questions.markingGuide: It measures the current through that path. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: How is a voltmeter connected?
questions.answerKey: In parallel across the component.
questions.markingGuide: It measures the potential difference between two points. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find resistance for 12 V and 3 A.
questions.answerKey: 4 Ω
questions.markingGuide: R=V/I. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find current for 8 V across 4 Ω.
questions.answerKey: 2 A
questions.markingGuide: I=V/R. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find series resistance of 3 Ω and 7 Ω.
questions.markingGuide: Add series resistances. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Does current get used up in a lamp?
questions.answerKey: No; energy is transferred while charge continues around the circuit.
questions.markingGuide: Distinguish charge flow from energy transfer. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find power for 9 V and 2 A.
questions.markingGuide: P=VI. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find energy for 20 W over 30 s.
questions.markingGuide: E=Pt. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Convert 500 W to kilowatts.
questions.answerKey: 0.5 kW

questions.content: Name three details needed in a request to use a room.
questions.answerKey: Purpose, date/time and the room or facility requested.
questions.markingGuide: A responsibility or contact detail can also help. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Does sending a request prove it has been approved?
